questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are logically equivalent?

I. $¬A∨B$

II. $A∧¬B$

III. $¬A∧B$
questions.worked_solution:
Two statements are logically equivalent if they have the same truth table. So, we construct a truth table for the three given statements:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬A∨B\,$ | $\,A∧¬B\,$ | $\,¬A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

We see that none of the statements have the same truth table, so none of them are logically equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "None of those listed".

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
¬(A∨¬B){{field-4}}¬A∧B
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∧B & ≡¬\text{T}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∧\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{T}$ and $B≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬A∧B & ≡¬\text{T}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}∧\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A≡\text{F}$ and $B≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∨¬B) & ≡¬(\text{F}∨¬\text{T}) \\  & ≡¬(\text{F}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡¬\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below.

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,¬(A∨¬B)\,$ | $\,¬A∧B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |

 

To determine whether $¬(A∨¬B)$ is logically equivalent to $¬A∧B,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{F},\text{F},\text{T},\text{F}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
¬(A∨¬B)≡¬A∧B.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the missing values in the following truth table:

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,Q∨¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-1}} | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | {{field-2}} | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | {{field-3}} |

Using your results, complete the following statement:

$$
Q∨¬(P∨Q){{field-4}}¬P∨Q
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's solve for the missing values:

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Q∨¬(P∨Q) & ≡\text{T}∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{T}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Q∨¬(P∨Q) & ≡\text{F}∨¬(\text{T}∨\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{F}∨¬\text{T} \\  & ≡\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{F}\end{aligned}
$$

- When $P≡\text{F}$ and $Q≡\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}¬P∨Q & ≡¬\text{F}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}∨\text{F} \\  & ≡\text{T}\end{aligned}
$$

Our completed table is shown below. 

| $\,P\,$ | $\,Q\,$ | $\,Q∨¬(P∨Q)\,$ | $\,¬P∨Q\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

To determine whether $Q∨¬(P∨Q)$ is logically equivalent to $¬P∨Q,$ we need to check whether their truth tables are equivalent.

Looking at the last two columns, we see that they are the same $(\text{T},\text{F},\text{T},\text{T}).$ Therefore, we conclude that 

$$
Q∨¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∨Q.
$$
